polyoxide-relay 0.37.1: BENIGN, Polymarket relay API client.
Predecessor: https://static.crates.io/crates/polyoxide-relay/polyoxide-relay-0.37.0.crate
Full unpacked diff: source, examples, tests and README unchanged; version, VCS
revision and polyoxide-core version/checksum changed. Fetched and diffed core
0.37.0/0.37.1 too: only gzip configuration changed from bool to Option<bool>,
restoring reqwest's default unless explicitly overridden, with matching tests.
Flagged keys construct local Alloy signers; transaction signatures and addresses
are sent to the relay, not raw private keys. No new hook, payload or export.

ioredis 4.9.5: BENIGN, Node.js Redis client.
Predecessor: https://registry.npmjs.org/ioredis/-/ioredis-4.9.4.tgz
Full unpacked diff: README unchanged, including NAT example 203.0.113.73;
version/changelog and built/cluster/index.js changed. Cluster refresh now chains
setTimeout callbacks rather than overlapping setInterval and queries CLUSTER
SLOTS on a duplicate connection, disconnecting afterward. This avoids blocking
commands such as BLPOP blocking topology refresh. Dependencies/scripts unchanged.
NAT mapping is caller-configured and socket targets are Redis endpoints.
Both alerts' evidence predates these releases: detection drift, not compromise.

Placement review: secret-name environment reads belong in os/env/secret-name,
not credential theft; IPv4 host properties belong in communications/ip/endpoint,
not proxy identification or traffic collection. Nearest leaves env/read and
ip/literal lose to the explicit secret name and endpoint host property.
Neither matcher establishes an attacker objective. Moves retain effective
file/platform scopes. Exact curl-wallet-transfer, browser relay and Telegram
consumers updated; broad objective directory selectors intentionally stop
counting these neutral observations as attack evidence. No legacy aliases.
Separate matcher fixes: Rust call nodes exclude comments/string examples;
host-table query rejects RFC 5737 ranges and invalid octets/leading zeros.
Resolver/private exclusions retained. Count is AST captures, not distinct hosts;
renamed description says multiple rather than five proxies.

Validation evidence: atomscan and cleave facts on both samples; source/call
inspection; complete predecessor diffs and Rust dependency diff; positive and
near-miss fixtures for signing reads, comments, IP host tables, resolvers,
documentation ranges and malformed addresses. Synthetic curl wallet export
still fires hostile; browser relay consumer still fires. Archive scans have
zero suspicious and zero hostile findings. No package-name allowlisting.

SkillTotal 0.61.1: BENIGN, static AI-component/package security scanner.
Sample SHA256: 0c24bdc8b4c32f0ddf20beda0fde68dd1b134897b41ae011f18971f0ad4e65b0
Fetched immediate predecessor 0.61.0 from PyPI:
https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/07/7e/50c83bebe5c7a39338d12d520443f00eefb3c9818d6b687376b290f8f31a/skilltotal-0.61.0-py3-none-any.whl
SHA256: 3cd54cd49210226087de386d7dc0b6749b8feb71dff4ce7398900deeccb7ae46
Full package-module comparison: only __init__.py version and agent_hook.py
change. The hook now includes finding file:line evidence in denial messages,
restricting attacker-controlled paths to plain characters before rendering.
python_ast.py is byte-identical to 0.61.0, so the detector example predates
0.61.1; the immediate predecessor is not the stated no-detection baseline.

Fetched and scanned 0.60.0 to locate the clean baseline:
https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/20/4e/0bf57c3a6939ac4bd9c6808032ad026d5c6a764839fb9a9baecace47c832/skilltotal-0.60.0-py3-none-any.whl
SHA256: b5964482be91b89c9e8bc8dace16b147a05858f6f2f0591f99786755b55a89c7
Its atomscan scan has zero suspicious/hostile traits. The full module diff
changes six of 51 source files: versions, denial-message rendering, local CI
classification, YAML action-command scalar parsing, network module detection,
and Python AST call/pickle-gadget recognition. The collector, sensitive-path
catalog, console entrypoint, and dependency declarations retain their behavior.
The astral.sh/uv/install.sh URL is an unchanged docstring showing commands
printed to a user; SkillTotal neither downloads nor executes it there.

Deciding evidence: python_ast.py:124-126 adds a COMMENT illustrating
getattr(__import__("os"), "sys" + "tem"). The nearby implementation recursively
resolves constant AST names and compares them with a dangerous-call set. It
never imports or invokes the analyzed target; scan() parses source with ast.parse
and visits nodes. The release extends static detection, not payload execution.
cleave facts confirms no such nested getattr/__import__ call in executable
syntax; actual getattr calls inspect AST node fields. Raw text regex was
misreading the new comment. No new payload, credential read/export, install
hook, or runtime network target is introduced by the diff.

Trait repair: split-name __import__/getattr requires a parsed nested call and
two string operands joined by +, retaining the concealment objective. Neutral
imported-module getattr also requires nested call syntax; relocated from
os/api-resolution/dynamic to metaprogramming/reflection with its exact Braodo
and multilayer consumers updated. No ancestor directory consumers select the
old home. This changes matching precision separately from placement; comments
and quoted examples no longer establish runtime reflection. Temporary-path
references are described as storage paths, not persistence. New ast.parse and
ast.walk call traits describe actual AST manipulation at notable criticality.
No package-identity allowlisting or severity-only suppression was added.

Lookup positive and near-miss controls: testdata/taxonomy/python-imported-getattr.
Real literal fragments match; whole names, variable suffixes and percent
formatting do not match concealment; comments/docstrings/strings match neither
concealment nor imported-module reflection. Ordinary getattr stays reflection
without claiming an import. AST calls and quoted AST examples have separate
positive/negative controls. Rescanned wheel: zero suspicious/hostile traits.
